statement: A discrete-time linear time-invariant system x(k+1) = Ax(k) + Bu(k) is controllable if and only if the n x nr controllability matrix C = [B  AB  A^2B  ...  A^(n-1)B] has full row rank, i.e., rank(C) = n, enabling any target state x(n) to be reached from initial state x(0) in n steps.

symbols.meaning: state vector at time step k
input (or control) vector at time step k
dimension of the control input vector

steps.text: Given the discrete-time state equation x(k+1) = Ax(k) + Bu(k) with initial state x(0) at k = 0, evaluate at the first step: x(1) = Ax(0) + Bu(0).
Substitute x(1) into the state equation at k = 1: x(2) = Ax(1) + Bu(1) = A(Ax(0) + Bu(0)) + Bu(1) = A^2 x(0) + ABu(0) + Bu(1).
Apply repeated back-substitutions of the state variable up to step n: x(n) = B u(n-1) + AB u(n-2) + ... + A^(n-1)B u(0) + A^n x(0).
Subtract A^n x(0) from both sides and collect the terms into a block-matrix product with the stacked input vector: x(n) - A^n x(0) = [B  AB  ...  A^(n-1)B] [u^T(n-1)  u^T(n-2)  ...  u^T(0)]^T.

For any imposed desired state x(n), the system can always be solved for the stacked vector of control vectors if and only if the matrix C = [B  AB  ...  A^(n-1)B] has full row rank, i.e., rank(C) = n.

assumptions.assumption: The system is a discrete linear time-invariant system governed by x(k+1) = Ax(k) + Bu(k) with constant matrices A and B.
assumptions.breaks_when: System matrices vary with time (time-varying dynamics) or system equations are nonlinear.

failure_modes.cause: The n x nr controllability matrix C lacks full row rank (i.e., it does not have n linearly independent columns), so its columns do not span the entire n-dimensional state space and arbitrary target states cannot be reached.
